application_order: Start with the recorded revisions unpatched, then invoke harness/evaluate.sh with the candidate.
The evaluator applies integration_patch at the CVA6 repository root to pulse configuration for prefetcher zero with base line 0x8001000
The evaluator applies directed_test_patch at the CVA6 repository root to reconstruct the directed program
The evaluator integrates the submitted module and reverses its integration patches on exit. Do not apply these patches before invocation.

reconstruction.reference_hdl: read rtl/src/hwpf_stride/hwpf_stride_wrapper.sv from HPDcache submodule f404e7ebbda8baa4af3729535f520a6b12a06d03, which CVA6 revision 6348e9e684678f83b40d0520028513d06b36e7b2 records
reconstruction.test_sources: The ordered patch records describe test provenance. Start with the pinned test sources and leave these patches unapplied before invoking harness/evaluate.sh, which reconstructs the tests.
reconstruction.address_mapping: The port test uses cache-line numbers and checks the generated physical request address.
reconstruction.evaluation: Start from an unpatched checkout and invoke harness/evaluate.sh with the candidate; the evaluator applies its own patches and restores its inputs.

evaluation_scope.port_scope: With base line 0, snoop unrelated line 300 and check that it produces no request, then snoop line 0 and observe five prefetches at line offsets 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 with stability during backpressure. Cycle offsets and internal identifiers are not acceptance requirements. A candidate that does not complete the observation within the cycle bound fails.
evaluation_scope.directed_scope: Access 0x80010000, the byte address of configured line 0x8001000, then compare complete retirement traces through the stride-arbiter comparator. The three cycle values are diagnostic observations and are not compared with fixed reference cycle counts.
evaluation_scope.reference_contract_exception: The fixed source identifies the target; its full-offset comparison and erased request tag are not imposed on a solver.
